form_analysis.feedback: Exceptional aftercare form for keloid management addressing this complex, recurrent condition. Provides comprehensive multimodal protocol combining laser with medical therapies. Outstanding emphasis on recurrence prevention, pressure therapy, and long-term maintenance. Realistic expectations about chronic management rather than cure.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser-assisted management of keloids - benign but aggressive scars that extend beyond original wound borders. Keloids have high recurrence rates and require MULTIMODAL therapy combining laser with medical treatments. This is CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT, not a one-time cure.

instructions.general_directive: Follow this strict protocol to minimize recurrence. Keloid management requires ongoing vigilance even after successful treatment.

sections.title: Keloid-Specific Considerations
items: HIGH RECURRENCE RISK: 40-100% without proper adjunctive therapy.
Common sites: Earlobes, chest, shoulders, back.
Genetic predisposition: More common in darker skin types.
Symptoms: Itching, pain, continued growth.

sections.title: Multimodal Treatment Protocol (ESSENTIAL)
items: 1. Laser: Vascular (PDL) for redness + Fractional for texture.
2. Intralesional Steroids: Triamcinolone injections during/after laser.
3. Pressure Therapy: Silicone sheets + pressure garments.
4. Topical Treatments: Imiquimod, 5-FU, retinoids.
ALL components must be used together for success.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Care
items: Increased redness, swelling, possible pinpoint bleeding.
Keloid may feel softer, less itchy within days.
Apply silicone gel immediately after healing (Day 5-7).
Begin pressure therapy as directed (often 12-24 hours daily).

sections.title: Recurrence Prevention (CRITICAL)
items: Pressure Therapy: Wear silicone sheets with compression 12-24 hours daily for 6-12 MONTHS minimum.
Steroid Injections: Scheduled every 4-8 weeks for 6+ months.
Avoid Trauma: No piercings, tattoos, or trauma to area.
Early Intervention: Treat ANY regrowth immediately.

sections.title: Medical Therapy Integration
items: Intralesional Steroids: Reduce inflammation, collagen production.
5-Fluorouracil (5-FU): Anti-proliferative, often combined with steroids.
Bleomycin: For resistant keloids.
Radiation Therapy: For high-risk keloids post-excision (rarely used).

sections.title: Complication Awareness
items: Rebound Growth: If therapy stopped too soon.
Skin Atrophy: From steroid overuse - report thin, shiny skin.
Hypopigmentation: Common with treatment.
Telangiectasia: From steroid injections or laser.

sections.title: Realistic Expectations
items: Goal: Flatten, soften, reduce symptoms - not necessarily complete elimination.
50-80% improvement with multimodal therapy.
Lifelong maintenance often required.
New keloids may form at other sites.
Follow-up every 3-6 months indefinitely.

sections.title: Genetic Counseling & Prevention
sections.content: If keloid-prone: Avoid elective procedures (piercings, tattoos). Treat acne early. Use silicone sheets prophylactically after any wound. Consider genetic testing if strong family history.

patient_declaration.reading_confirmation: Keloid management requires lifelong commitment to prevention and treatment.
patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Ask about the full multimodal plan including injections and pressure therapy.
patient_declaration.declaration_text: I understand keloids have high recurrence rates and require ongoing multimodal therapy, possibly for life.
